authorization: MAIN 2026-09-11 item (1): delete ntb2's certified-and-moved AP bulk under sr5's certify-or-block rule

classes.measured_reason: Two rows totalling 3,780,374,400 B -- 99.2% of the class -- record sha256 as the literal string 'SKIPPED_LARGE_STREAMED'. There is no hash, so no certificate can bind the bytes on disk to the manifest, and no rebuild can be checked against anything. The rule is explicit: if the proof is missing, emit a blocker and keep the bytes. The remaining 64 rows total only 30,732,148 B and are not worth a producer.
classes.second_reason: Its rebuild command is a full deterministic decode (experiments/ddm_ntb2_public.py --treatment frame_even), which is candidate work this charter bars and could not be exercised here.

classes.refused_reason: run_completed is FALSE on six of the twelve rows. Their stated justification -- 'superseded by the run's own RESULT.json + argmax_plane.npz' -- is not true for a run that did not complete, so the supersession claim fails and the bytes stay.
classes.certifiable_reason: Six rows have run_completed TRUE, a real sha256, and BOTH superseding artifacts verified present on Vertigo for every treatment: blocks.1.film.weight, blocks.3.film.weight and control each have RESULT.json and argmax_plane.npz under /Volumes/VertigoDataTier/pact/ddm_ntb2_non_tail_lossy_levers/renderer_score/<treatment>/.
classes.why_sr5_did_not_delete_them: Their certificate is a SUPERSESSION proof, not a rebuild proof -- the recorded rebuild command is a renderer_score run this charter bars -- so neither sr5 producer fits, and 354 MB does not justify a fifth producer once the rlc2 relocation had already returned 5.84 GiB to APDataStore. The six verified rows are handed forward so a successor can act in one step.
